extraction.Name: Lillian A. Lawyer
extraction.Refused/Protested: a fee patent covering her entire allotment containing 320 acres was issued in her name without her consent or application; that it was not her intention ever to ask the Government to issue patent in fee for the same as she had her home on the same
extraction.Recorded patent: fee patent was duly recorded at Hot Springs, South Dakota
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: the land covered by the said patent was sold for $3250.00 during the year 1919 to Harry Evans; that this land was never mortgaged
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she could not keep the land and pay out for taxes when there was no income derived therefrom; the reason the land was sold was because she could not profitably look after the payment of taxes and keep off Indians from the use of the land
extraction.Fee Patent Date: sometime during the years of 1918 or 1919
extraction.Occupation/Income: working for the Government as Seamstress; husband also employed in Government service
extraction.NOTES: Resident of Nez Perce County, Idaho for the past 22 years; allotment contained 320 acres; patent mailed to her and she signed receipts and returned them to the Agency office; affiant believes consideration was fair value for the land; sold not on account of settlement of old debt or taxes or any other encumbrances; amount paid for taxes have never been refunded; mental and physical condition are normal; financial status is good; Government, County and State have never contributed anything towards her support; has three children dependent upon her; husband assists in support of minor children; owing to husband's employment in Idaho she was forced to leave Pine Ridge; had constructed three room frame house, barn for five head of horses and one cow, well drilled and fenced entire allotment at a total cost of $905.00; would be glad to repurchase land at same rate provided improvements were in same condition; had Government retained allotment in trust she would still be the owner; affidavit sworn December 4, 1928 before notary Starr J. Maxwell
